newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan December foreign currency deposits fall.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan December foreign currency deposits fall.

text.p: Taiwan's outstanding foreign currency deposits fell to T$309.8 billion at end-December from T$323.6 billion a month earlier, the central bank said on Monday.

The bank attributed the fall mainly to a slowing of fund inflows for joint-venture investment and local firms' corporate bond issues abroad in December. Such inflows had emerged in November, the bank said in a statement.

Deposits had been at high levels recently because exporters, seeking to limit risk in exchanging foreign currency, gradually had been shifted to pay for raw material imports directly with foreign currency rather than Taiwan dollars, central bank officials had said.
Foreign currency deposits began rising in mid-1995 as political frictions between Taiwan and arch-rival China intensified.

China, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province, mounted wargames and missile tests in waters near the island in the second half of 1995 and early 1996 in a warning against moves to secure the island's indepedence.

An intensification of tensions in the months before Taiwan's historic direct presidential election in March 1996 sparked a run on U.S. currency, big cash outflows and sharp rises in foreign exchange holdings.
Because much of the capital that was exchanged into foreign currency during the crisis stayed in Taiwan deposits, the capital outflows were not so serious as feared, central bank officials have said.
